param_schema.name: exec_risk_pct

param_schema.name: exec_sl_level

Wider stop, smaller position, more room

param_schema.name: exec_sl_deep

param_schema.desc: On = an entry filling at 0.786 or deeper puts its stop right back at the start of the move, giving it more room.
param_schema.disable_note: No effect — the stop is already 1.0, so both states place it in the same spot.

param_schema.name: exec_sl_buf_tk
param_schema.label: Stop buffer beyond the level (ticks)
param_schema.desc: Extra room beyond the stop level, in ticks, so a wick through it does not take you out.

More room for wicks, wider risk per trade

param_schema.name: exec_min_stop_mode

param_schema.name: exec_min_stop_val

param_schema.desc: The floor itself, in whatever unit the setting above uses. Higher refuses more setups.

Refuses real trades, not just dangerous ones

param_schema.name: exec_be_arm_r
param_schema.label: Any trade moves to breakeven at (R)
param_schema.desc: When ANY trade's stop moves to protect it, measured on how far price has gone its way as a multiple of the trade's own risk. -1 (default) is off, which is the shipped behaviour: the only thing that moves the stop is price TOUCHING a rung on the ladder, so a trade can run a full R in profit, turn around and pay the full loss with nothing having happened — the re-entry short of 2020-11-04 did exactly that at 1.016R with its nearest rung at 1.25R. MEASURED 2026-08-25 over 6.6 years on 246 trades: every setting tested LOST money against leaving it off — 139.09R off, against 99.92R at 1.00, 71.20R at 0.75 and 51.55R at 0.50. At 1.00 it rescued 17 trades worth +17.07R and destroyed 15 worth -54.49R, one of them a +16.48R winner cut to +0.35R. Win rate rose 58% to 69% while the money fell by two thirds, which is the fingerprint of cutting winners. Lab only, and it is kept as a recorded dead end.
guide: Off — the stop holds until a rung is touched
Protects every trade earlier

param_schema.name: exec_be_keep_r
param_schema.label: Protected stop keeps (R) of risk
param_schema.desc: How FAR the stop moves when the row above arms it. 0 (default) is all the way to breakeven. A positive number leaves that share of the trade's own entry risk in the market, so a trade that is protected and then turns around pays part of the loss rather than none of it. MEASURED 2026-08-25: it is the least bad version and still worse than off — 118.99R at 1.00 and 108.12R at 0.75 against 139.09R off, and at 0.75 the worst drawdown got WORSE (60.21% against 53.68%). Must be under 1 — at 1 the stop lands back on the entry stop and does nothing while reading as switched on. Does nothing on its own. Lab only.
guide: All the way to breakeven
Leaves more risk in the market

param_schema.name: exec_tp1_pct

guide: More size left for the runner
Bank more early, smaller runner

param_schema.name: exec_tp2_pct

guide: Bigger runner
Bank more at TP2, smaller runner

param_schema.name: exec_be_buf_tk

guide: True breakeven
Locks in more, stopped out sooner

param_schema.name: exec_be_buf_mode

guide: Ticks — same distance whatever the trade risks
Fraction of stop + cost — scales, and never exits at a loss

param_schema.name: exec_be_buf_r
param_schema.label: Breakeven buffer (fraction of stop)
param_schema.desc: The cushion as a share of what the trade risked. 0.20 is one fifth of the stop. Only read when the buffer mode is not ticks.
guide: Close to breakeven
Locks in more, stopped out sooner

param_schema.name: exec_be_cost_margin_r

param_schema.desc: How far the stop clears the trade's own costs by. 0 exits exactly flat after costs; anything above banks a little. Only read in the cost-covering mode.

Keeps more, stopped out sooner

param_schema.name: exec_be_cap_pct

param_schema.name: exec_be_cost_conflict

Clamp — smaller loss than the full stop

param_schema.name: exec_runner_trail

Structure + ratchet — keeps more of each run

param_schema.name: exec_struct_trail_buf_tk
param_schema.label: Structure trail buffer (ticks)
param_schema.desc: How many ticks beyond the last swing the trailing stop sits, so a wick through it does not clip you.

Wide of the swing — survives noise, gives back more

param_schema.name: exec_trail_pct

param_schema.desc: How big each trailing step is, as a percent of price rather than dollars, so it means the same at any price.

Too big — barely does anything

param_schema.name: exec_trail_step
param_schema.label: Runner trail step ($ of price)
param_schema.desc: The step size in dollars. On gold 1 pip is 10 cents, so 50 pips = 5.0.

Looser trail — lets winners breathe, gives back more

param_schema.name: exec_tp2_stop_mode

param_schema.desc: Where the stop jumps to the moment the second target is hit. TP1 is tight and can scratch the trade; breakeven gives it the most room.
guide: TP1 price — protects the gain, scratches runners
Breakeven — maximum room for the runner

param_schema.name: exec_scale_in

param_schema.name: exec_scale_mode

param_schema.desc: Where it adds. Trail buys at market the moment the trailing stop moves up; BOS retest waits for the next break of structure and rests an order at the level that broke.

BOS retest — waits for a pullback that often never comes; loses money outside 2020

param_schema.name: exec_scale_max_adds
param_schema.label: How many times it may add
param_schema.desc: The most times one trade may add. It only adds again once the trailing stop has moved up since the last add, so a stalling trade gets nothing.
guide: Fewer adds — smaller position, shallower drawdown
More adds — bigger runners, more given back

param_schema.name: exec_scale_cap_x
param_schema.label: Biggest add, as a multiple of the original size
param_schema.desc: A ceiling on each add, as a multiple of the size the trade opened with. 1.0 means an add can never be bigger than the original position.
guide: Lower — this is the drawdown lever; 0.5 is the measured best
Higher — more return bought with much more drawdown, and more gap exposure

param_schema.name: exec_scale_tp_mode

param_schema.desc: Where the added lots bank. Ride leaves them on the trailing stop with the rest of the trade, which is how every run before 2026-08-19 behaved. The other three rest them at the nearest level of that kind price has not already taken, and only when it sits beyond the newest add, so every lot banks in profit. It moves the ADDS only — the base trade's stop and partials are untouched.
guide: Ride — the default, and measured best (194.15R); the adds earn on the few trades that run a long way
Prev week H/L — costs 25.64R (168.51R), OUTSIDE this strategy's own 15.06R noise
Prev day / H4 — worse again (157.57R / 146.09R), and worse the more often the level gets hit

param_schema.name: exec_time_stop_mode
param_schema.label: Time stop
param_schema.desc: Closes a trade open longer than the hours below. Before TP1 only fires while the trade has never reached the first target.
guide: Off — the clock never closes a trade
Always — the clock closes winners too

param_schema.name: exec_time_stop_hrs
param_schema.label: Time stop (hours)
param_schema.desc: How long a trade may stay open, in hours, weekends included. About 24 to 40 hours all give the same answer.
guide: Cuts winners as well as losers
Fires on almost nothing

param_schema.name: exec_close_opp_sos
param_schema.label: Close on opposite SOS
param_schema.desc: On = close the trade early if structure breaks back the other way. Off = let the stop or a target resolve it.

param_schema.name: exec_secondary
param_schema.label: Secondary re-entries
param_schema.desc: Adds a second entry off a FASTER chart than the strategy trades — the fill clock set below, 5 minutes by default: once the first trade is safe at breakeven and price falls back into the zone, it re-enters for the same targets. On by default. MEASURED over 7.9 years on the settings that now ship: 54 re-entries, worth +13.9R on top of the first trades' +206.2R, and the first trades are untouched to the decimal. It is bought with drawdown — the worst peak-to-trough goes from 51.8% to 60.4% — and it leans hard on one trade, which is why it is sized at half. Lab only, and slower to run than a plain backtest.

param_schema.name: exec_sec_trigger
param_schema.label: What triggers a re-entry
param_schema.desc: What has to happen before a re-entry places its order. FVG in zone (default) needs no structure event at all — while the setup is alive and price is back in the zone, it rests the order at the SAME fair-value-gap price the first trade would have used. Structure shift is the original rule: a break of structure on the fill clock, then an order at a 38.2% pullback of that move. MEASURED: the shift confirms late. On 29 October 2025 it did not confirm until an hour after the low, its order missed by $8 and price ran a hundred points without it; a gap sat in the zone and price traded into it an hour earlier. Reclaim Entry is the only one of the three built for a trade that LOST: the first trade is stopped at the deep edge of the entry band, price does not go on to break the move, and instead comes back up through that level — an order then waits AT the level for the retest, stopping at the far end of the move. Because those two levels sit close together the risk is a fraction of the first trade's, so the same cash buys a much bigger position. It reads its OWN four settings below rather than the shared ones, so it means the same thing whether it runs alone or alongside the gap. MEASURED: waiting for the retest earned +43R over 7.9 years while chasing the reclaim earned nothing, so the wait is the whole edge. The fourth choice runs the gap and the reclaim TOGETHER. That is safe because they cover opposite outcomes — a first trade either reaches breakeven or is stopped out, never both — so they can never want the same setup. MEASURED over 7.9 years: 107 re-entries between them, none sharing a setup and none overlapping another in time, and the two together are exactly the two apart. It requires the gap half set to Breakeven and the reclaim half to Stopped only, and refuses any other pairing. Lab only.

param_schema.name: exec_sec_zone_deep
param_schema.label: Secondary zone — deep edge
param_schema.desc: How deep into the retrace the re-entry may still arm, as a fib ratio. 0.886 (default) is the entry band's own edge. 1.0 is the start of the leg, which lets it arm while price has closed BEYOND the band — the state a swept stop leaves behind. It does not move the re-entry's stop. Lab only.

param_schema.name: exec_sec_zone_shallow
param_schema.label: Secondary zone — shallow edge
param_schema.desc: The shallow end of that same zone, as a fib ratio. 0.618 (default) is the entry band's edge. A smaller number lets the re-entry arm after price has already reclaimed part of the move — more chances, at a worse price relative to the targets. Lab only.

param_schema.name: exec_sec_max_wait_bars
param_schema.label: Cancel a resting re-entry after (fill-clock bars)
param_schema.desc: How long a resting re-entry order may wait unfilled before it is taken off the book. 0 (default) never cancels, which is the shipped behaviour: the order rests at its price until the setup that armed it dies. Counted in FILL-CLOCK bars, so it moves with the fill clock above — at a 5-minute clock, 144 is 12 hours. Once cancelled, that setup cannot place the order again; a fresh break of structure arms a new one. MEASURED 2026-08-23 over 6.6 years: 61 of 90 re-entry orders fill inside 30 minutes, and every cutoff of 6 hours or less loses money because the 6-to-12-hour band is the best in the book (4 wins from 5, +11.25R). Past 12 hours the book has never won — 8 orders, 8 losses, worth +8.00R to cancel, on 8 trades. Lab only.
guide: Never cancels — it waits for the setup to die
Gives up on the order sooner

param_schema.name: exec_sec_risk_pct
param_schema.label: Re-entry risk (% of the first trade's)
param_schema.desc: How much a re-entry risks, as a percentage of what a first trade risks. 50 (default) is half; 100 is the same. It changes the SIZE only — entry, stop and targets are identical, so the R figure a re-entry reports does not move at all and must be scaled by this number before it is compared with a first trade's. MEASURED over 7.9 years: the re-entries add 6.9R at a quarter, 13.9R at half, 20.9R at three-quarters and 27.8R at full weight, and the worst peak-to-trough goes 56.2 / 60.4 / 64.4 / 68.1 per cent against 51.8 with them off — a straight line with no natural stopping place, so half was chosen because one trade is three quarters of the whole leg's profit. Zero is refused: use the on/off switch instead. Lab only.

param_schema.name: exec_sec_req_div
param_schema.label: Re-entry needs a divergence
param_schema.desc: Whether a re-entry also needs a live RSI divergence on the 15-minute chart, on top of the setup still being alive and price being back in the zone. Not needed (default). It is NOT the same question as what arms the first trade — the bot ships finding its trades from liquidity sweeps, so the divergence is usually absent and requiring it stops re-entries firing at all: MEASURED over the year to 2026-08-18, zero re-entries with it required. Lab only.

param_schema.name: exec_sec_req_m1_dir
param_schema.label: Fill-clock trend must agree
param_schema.desc: On = a re-entry only arms while the structure on the FILL CLOCK (the faster feed set below, 5 minutes by default) is already pointing the trade's way. This is the "has structure shifted against me" test on the lower timeframe. MEASURED: it drops 2 of 7 re-entries and does not filter the one full loss. Lab only.

param_schema.name: exec_sec_be_at
param_schema.label: Re-entry moves to breakeven at
param_schema.desc: When a re-entry's stop jumps to breakeven. TP1 (default) is the same rule the first trade uses. TP2 holds the original stop for longer, giving the trade room to breathe. MEASURED: TP2 is WORSE — the three trades it saved from a breakeven scratch each became a full loss instead. Lab only.

param_schema.name: exec_sec_once_per_setup
param_schema.label: One re-entry per primary
param_schema.desc: How often one setup may be re-entered. On = once. Off = once per signal on the fill clock, which is what once let a single setup be re-entered twice about an hour and a half apart. It resets on a fresh break of structure. Lab only.

param_schema.name: exec_sec_max_per_setup
param_schema.label: ↳ How many re-entries per setup
param_schema.desc: Read only when One re-entry per primary is ON. How many times one setup may be re-entered before it is done. A re-entry that is STOPPED OUT still ends the setup whatever this says, so raising it only lets a setup be re-tried after a scratch. MEASURED over 6.6 years: 2, 3, 5 and unlimited all produce the same book — only one setup ever offered a second re-entry, and it lost. Lab only.

param_schema.name: exec_sec_rest_and_leave
param_schema.label: Rest the re-entry order and leave it
param_schema.desc: Once the re-entry's order is placed it stays there, at the price it was placed at. It only comes off if the setup that placed it dies, the trade fills, or the leg is finished. Off re-decides the order from scratch on every bar, so any one condition closing pulls it back off the book — which is what made the order need re-checking every minute.

param_schema.name: exec_sec_fill_tf_min
param_schema.label: Re-entry fill clock (minutes)
param_schema.desc: Which bars the backtest fills the re-entry's resting order against. It changes how accurate the test is, not how the strategy trades — live, the broker fills at the price that trades. A coarser setting fills you worse than really happened, so the result reads worse than it is. Smaller is more faithful and much slower to load.

param_schema.name: exec_rec_require
param_schema.label: Reclaim needs the first trade to have…
param_schema.desc: What the first trade on this setup must have done before Reclaim Entry may re-enter. Stopped only (default) is the whole point of that trigger — it re-enters a setup whose first trade was stopped out at the deep edge. It is separate from the shared setting above so the gap trigger and the reclaim can run together wanting opposite things of the same trade; when they do, this must stay on Stopped only and the shared one on Breakeven, because those are the only two that cannot both be true of one setup. Lab only.
param_schema.disable_note: No effect — the trigger above is not Reclaim Entry, so nothing reads this.

param_schema.name: exec_rec_stop
param_schema.label: Reclaim stop sits at
param_schema.desc: Where Reclaim Entry's stop goes. Only these two, because the reclaim enters at a fixed price and a swing on the fill clock can land on either side of it — a stop that is sometimes above and sometimes below the thing it protects is not a stop, so the fill-clock anchors are refused rather than substituted. 1.0 is the default and is the reason the trigger exists: the start of the move sits a median 0.43 of the original risk past the deep edge, so the same cash buys a much bigger position. Lab only.
param_schema.disable_note: No effect — the trigger above is not Reclaim Entry, so nothing reads this.

param_schema.name: exec_rec_tp_r
param_schema.label: Reclaim's first target, in R
param_schema.desc: Where Reclaim Entry's first target sits, as a multiple of its own risk. -1 uses the halfway fib instead, like the first trade. MEASURED over 7.9 years and the ladder matters as much as the number: taking the whole position off at 3x made 7,225x, where banking half at 1.25x — the gap trigger's ladder — made 3,111x, which is worse than taking no re-entry at all. A re-entry priced this tight has to be allowed to pay for the ones that fail. param_schema.name: exec_sec_tp2_x

The first target is a multiple of the trade's own risk while the second stays the 15-minute swing level it was armed on, so the two are measured by different rulers and the second can land nearer than the first. -1 (default) is off and the swing level stands. A positive number places the second target at that multiple of the first one's distance from entry, on EVERY re-entry, so the two are always in order. The difference from the floor setting above is direction: the floor only ever pushes a target further away and lets the swing level win when it is already out there, while this one also pulls IN a target that ran to nearly seven times the trade's risk. It does NOT move where profit banks — the second target takes nothing off on the shipped ladder, so what changes is when the stop lifts to the first target's price and hands the rest to the trail. That cuts both ways: on a trade whose swing level was the NEARER of the two, moving it out delays the point where the trade becomes unloseable. Lab only. MEASURED 2026-08-25 over 6.5 years on gold, PU Prime ECN with real fills, commission and swap: off = 139.09R at 53.68% worst drawdown; 1.1x = 142.83R at 47.95%; 1.25x = 142.87R at 47.95%; 1.5x = 141.09R at 49.02%; 2x = 140.29R at 50.67%; 2.5x = 139.79R at 51.11%. It has a real cost: three trades whose swing level was the nearer of the two rungs lose the only thing that moved their stop to breakeven, and each goes from a small win to a full loss.

Each recovery trade is sized off a balance holding every main trade that had closed by then, so that half is real - what is missing is the way back: the main trades never see the recovery profit, so it sits beside the equity curve instead of lifting it and never compounds. /strategies/sos_fade.edge: It trades reversals, but only once the market has proved the turn. First price runs the stops past a recent high or low. Then structure breaks the other way, which is the confirmation. Then it waits for a deep pullback and leaves a limit order sitting there — it never chases. Most of the money comes from the part of the trade that is left to run.

steps.label: 01 · Arm
steps.title: Something runs out of steam
steps.detail: Price runs the stops past a recent high or low. That is what puts a setup on the watchlist. A momentum divergence at an extreme can do it too, but that is off by default.

steps.label: 02 · Confirm
steps.title: Structure breaks the other way
steps.detail: The market breaks back the other way soon after. Without that the setup is only a guess, so it never arms.

steps.label: 03 · Zone
steps.title: Wait for the pullback
steps.detail: Price comes back deep into the move and a gap left behind sits in the same place. A limit order rests there and waits to be filled. It is never a chase.

steps.label: 04 · Manage
steps.title: Let it run
steps.detail: Touching the first target moves the stop to breakeven, so the trade can no longer lose. By default nothing is banked early — the whole position rides out on the trailing stop.
